judged_text: The `raw_html` cook_method short-circuits `cook` by returning `raw` unmodified, which changes the contract of `Post#cooked` from 'sanitized rendered HTML' to 'whatever bytes were stored' for an entire class of posts. Every consumer of #cooked outside this diff's embed view — notification emails, search indexing, excerpts, serializations to clients — now receives raw externally-sourced HTML for imported posts; each existing caller inherits unparsed markup (e.g., tags visible in emails/search text) and the next feature that trusts `cooked` being sanitized silently breaks for these rows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline for those posts. `TopicEmbed.import` and `Jobs::PollFeed` feed/import externally sourced HTML (`doc.content` from `ruby-readability`, and `i.content` from RSS) into `PostCreator` with `cook_method: :raw_html`, so the resulting `post.cooked` becomes whatever raw HTML was stored, without any sanitization/processing shown in this diff. That is a real behavioral change for `#cooked` for imported posts and can leak raw/unsafe markup into any place that uses `post.cooked` (the new embed view even does `raw post.cooked`).
